# Panelary

> The best methods for panel data. Leak-safe, Polars-native feature engineering and ML for panel data (many entities observed over time). Panelary is a panel-first (entity x time) data-science toolkit with an sklearn-familiar API, lazy Polars execution, and correctness-by-construction: no lookahead, ever. Version 0.5.0 is pure Python (the Rust extension was dropped in 0.4.0) and ships a single universal `py3-none-any` wheel with `py.typed`. Built on the foundations of functime (Apache-2.0) and licensed Apache-2.0.

Workflow: impute -> engineer -> label -> select -> reduce -> model -> validate, with no lookahead at any stage.

Project URLs:
- Documentation: https://sovai-research.github.io/panelary/
- Repository: https://github.com/sovai-research/panelary
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/panelary/

## Naming and install

- Project/brand name: Panelary. PyPI distribution and Python import name: `panelary` (one name, no alias). The conventional import is `import panelary as pn`. The pre-0.4.0 names `polars_features` and `PanelKit` are retired and no longer resolve.
- Requires Python >= 3.10. Mandatory dependencies are only `numpy` and `polars>=1.0.0`; everything heavier is an optional extra.
- Install: `pip install panelary`, or `pip install "panelary[recommended]"` for the batteries-included set (`ml`, `scipy`, `seasonality`, `cafe`), or `[all]` for every real feature extra. There are 23 extras: `ml`, `scipy`, `progress`, `seasonality`, `forecasting`, `automl`, `lightgbm`, `catboost`, `xgboost`, `ann`, `fast`, `llm`, `gpu`, `viz`, `cafe`, `dimreduce`, `explain`, `schema`, `fuzzy`, the bundles `recommended` and `all`, and the toolchains `docs` and `dev`.
- A missing optional dependency raises an actionable error naming the extra to install (via `panelary._internal._deps.require`), never a bare ImportError.

## The golden path

Each workflow stage has one top-level verb on the `pn` namespace, fronting the subpackage that does the work. Reach for the underlying classes for the full parameter surface.

- `pn.impute` — point-in-time imputation (CAFE and simpler baselines).
- `pn.features` — bulk and per-column leak-safe feature generation.
- `pn.select` — feature selection under purged cross-validation.
- `pn.reduce` — latent factors and dimensionality reduction.
- `pn.cluster` — time-series and cross-sectional clustering.
- `pn.regression` — panel regression and panel-aware ML estimators.
- `pn.causal` — causal and econometric panel estimators.
- `pn.bubbles` — explosive-behaviour and change-point detection.

## Core concepts

- PanelFrame: a typed, lazy view over a long-format panel keyed by `(entity, time)`. Construct with `pn.PanelFrame(df, entity="ticker", time="date")`; read back via `.entity_col` / `.time_col`. The unit of work is the panel, not a bag of rows.
- panel_safe contract: within-entity operations stay inside their entity and run in time order (`.over(entity_col)` on a time-sorted panel).
- leakage_safe contract: cross-sectional operations are per-date (`.over(time_col)`), and anything with a `fit` step is fit per fold on training data only — never globally, never on the test fold.
- Prefix invariance: `f(x[:T])[t] == f(x[:T+k])[t]` for `t <= T`. No window size, threshold, lag order or normalisation constant may depend on total series length.
- Leak-safe Pipeline: sklearn-style `fit`/`transform` pipeline where scalers and selectors are fit per fold.
- Purged cross-validation: `PurgedKFold` and `CombinatorialPurgedCV` (CPCV) apply purging and embargo to remove train/test leakage around fold boundaries. `embargo` / `horizon` take integers (time steps) or calendar durations (`"5d"`, `"1mo"`, `timedelta`, business days `"5bd"` / `BusinessDays`).
- Point-in-time join: `pn.asof_join` (also `PanelFrame.asof_join`) is bitemporal — each row `(entity, t)` sees a vintage only once `knowledge_time + lag <= t`.
- Expression namespaces: operators are called as `pl.col(...).<namespace>.<name>(...)` across the `panel`, `xs`, `ts` and `factor` namespaces. `.panel` implies `.over(entity)`; `.xs` implies `.over(time)`. Typed `.pyi` stubs ship in the wheel.
- Operator registry: `pn.registry` holds a `FeatureSpec` per operator recording signature, input/output shape, tier, `panel_safe`/`leakage_safe` flags, and provenance/license. `registry.to_records()` serialises it, `registry.to_llms_txt()` renders a machine-readable operator catalogue, and `registry.audit()` checks that every operator is permissively licensed. 56 operators are registered today (`ts`=42, `xs`=7, `factor`=4, `panel`=3).

## Shipped modules (0.5.0)

- `pn.core` — the correctness kernel: `PanelFrame`, leak-safe `Pipeline`, `PanelTransformer`/`PanelEstimator` protocols, purged model selection.
- `pn.transform` — panel-native, leak-safe preprocessing transformers: `TimeSeriesScaler`, `CrossSectionalScaler`, `CrossSectionalRank`, `Neutralize`, `FracDiff`.
- `pn.label` — leak-safe labeling (Lopez de Prado, AFML Ch. 3): `triple_barrier` and friends.
- `pn.select` — leak-safe feature selection (supervised and unsupervised), fit per fold.
- `pn.factor` — cross-sectional factor evaluation: information coefficients, neutralization, portfolio construction.
- `pn.reduce` — leak-safe dimensionality reduction: PCA, ICA, hierarchical factor analysis, robust factors, factor-count selection.
- `pn.cluster` — leak-safe panel clustering, including cross-sectional and k-Shape.
- `pn.econ` — panel and time-series econometrics: HDFE, Fama-MacBeth, IVX, DML, connectedness, plus an econometric feature suite (EVT, HAR-RV, liquidity, long memory, Nelson-Siegel, unit roots).
- `pn.explain` — leak-safe, panel-aware feature attribution (SHAP): tree and estimator backends, interactions, stability, aggregation.
- `pn.validation` — honest validation and selection: bootstraps, CV, forecast tests, selection statistics.
- `pn.detect` — causal detection of explosive regimes, bubbles and change points (GSADF/BSADF, CUSUM/FOCuS monitors, panel breadth).
- `pn.forecasting` / `pn.models` — forecaster and panel/cross-sectional model wrappers (linear, kNN, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, AutoML, conformal, censored).
- `pn.metrics`, `pn.evaluation`, `pn.backtesting` — point, probabilistic and multi-objective metrics; deflated Sharpe ratio; probability of backtest overfitting.
- `pn.seasonality` — calendar and Fourier seasonal features.
- `pn.catch22`, `pn.feature_extractors`, `pn.extract_features` — time-series feature extraction, including a clean-room catch22 reimplementation.
- `pn.imputation` / `pn.CafeImputer` — leak-safe imputation.
- `pn.llm` — optional LLM-assisted analysis of panels.
- `pn.leakage` — the point-in-time compiler (`causalize`, `audit`, `audit_features` for a whole feature set) and the borrowed-accuracy metric: an executed do-Shapley decomposition, per-seed replicates, opt-in permutation sampling beyond 12 components. Results serialise with a byte-deterministic `to_json()`.
- `pn.select.refit_shapley` — Shapley value of feature groups or data sources, by refitting through a purged splitter.
- `pn.quality` — data validation before anything is fitted: panel invariants, column contracts, fitted-state provenance, near-duplicate straddle checks (`PanelValidator`, `validate_panel`, `quality_report`; also `df.panel.validate()`).
- `pn.clean` — point-in-time dedup (exact / MinHash / SimHash; a row goes only if it copies an earlier one), split-aware CV helpers, canonicalisation, survivorship, train-fitted outlier cleaning, entity resolution (also `df.panel.dedup()`).
- `pn.synth` — seeded synthetic panels with planted ground truth (`generate_panel`, `SynthConfig`, `sample_config`), bitemporal vintages, and `check_planted_lag`, a leak detector keyed to the planted signal's known lag.
- `pn.shape` — shape algebra: compress / lift / factorize / sketch a named axis; trailing time-axis transforms by default (PAA, Spectral, Delay), numpy randomized PCA, seeded sparse/SRHT projections, real-column ID/CUR, partial Tucker; `explain()` and `plan()` budgets. Also via `pn.reduce(method="rsvd"|...)` and `pn.features(method="delay"|"spectral")`.
- `pn.embed` — leak-safe numerical embeddings from trailing windows: `QuantEmbedder`, `RandIntC22`, `HydraEmbedder`, `RandomFourierFeatures`, `TensorSketch` (stateless, `fit_is_empty` enforced), `CausalMiniRocket` (prefix-safe MiniRocket-PPV), `CrossRocket` (random operators across the cross-section), `EmbeddingCompressor`, `PreValidatedRidge`, `CrossSectionalEmbedder`; `pn.catch22.catch22_batch` for vectorised catch22.
- `pn.assert_no_lookahead`, `pn.testing` — the leakage verifier and test helpers.

## Ecosystem positioning

- Complements polars-ds and polars_ta (general Polars-native primitives); does not compete with them.
- Nixtla (statsforecast/mlforecast) owns general forecasting; Panelary centers on leak-safe feature engineering, labeling, selection, attribution and cross-sectional ML for panels.
- catch22 features are clean-room reimplemented from Lubba et al. (2019), NOT vendored from the GPL `pycatch22`.
